title: Pinned failover ledger and stable handoff protocol for model version deprecation
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: Customers pin service routes to specific model versions for strict compatibility guarantees. When a pinned version is deprecated or becomes unhealthy in a region, current behavior either (a) blocks requests (poor availability) or (b) falls back to an ad-hoc variant (risking silent quality regressions). We need a robust, auditable, and customer-configurable policy that handles regional outages and planned deprecations while preserving SLOs, minimizing quality regressions, and providing clear signals to customers.

Goal: Implement a 'Pinned Failover Ledger' and 'Stable Handoff Protocol' that: (1) records deterministic fallback decisions in an immutable ledger for observability/audit, (2) exposes configuration for controlled graceful handoffs (grace_period, downgrade_tolerance, allowed_variant_list), (3) coordinates deprecation windows with traffic shaping and customer notifications, (4) integrates with performance profile publishing so the system only selects fallback variants that meet declared latency/quality bounds.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A failover ledger entry is created for every fallback decision containing timestamp, source model pin, chosen fallback variant, region, reason, and SLO impact estimate.
2) New API fields accepted on Pin objects: grace_period_days, fallback_sequence, enforce_profile_thresholds (boolean).
3) Routing honors fallback_sequence and will not auto-escalate to variants that fail published performance profiles unless customer allows downgrade.
4) Deprecation flow supports: planned deprecation (with configured grace period + automatic traffic rampdown), emergency deprecation (immediate but recorded with forced safe fallback), and manual override by customer.
5) End-to-end tests simulate regional outage and planned deprecation proving zero-request-loss for routes with fallback enabled, and alerts generated when fallback SLO impact > 5% error budget.
6) Console surfaces ledger entries and a per-pin timeline in Rollouts/Pin management UI.
7) Docs and runbook published before release.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions: use a write-ahead ledger stored in the control plane (append-only) keyed by pin_id + monotonic sequence to keep fallbacks auditable and replayable. Ledger entries are small JSON blobs stored in our existing metadata store (use current write pattern to ensure transactions).

Routing behavior: when a request arrives for a pinned model version: check health & regional capacity; if healthy, route. If unhealthy, consult pin.fallback_sequence (ordered list of variant IDs + region preference). For each candidate, validate against published performance profile (latency P95, quality regression score threshold) unless enforce_profile_thresholds == false. Stop at first acceptable variant. Record ledger entry with chosen variant and metadata. If no candidate acceptable, route to customer-configured fallback policy: reject / queue (respecting latency budgets) / route to best-effort variant (and mark as 'downgrade').

Deprecation flow: additions to the onboarding API to publish deprecation windows and associated recommended replacement models. When deprecation is planned: create deprecation_notice (start_date, end_of_grace, recommended_replacements). After start_date: traffic shaping begins; system sends automated pin-level notification emails and adds advisory ledger entries per pin impacted. During grace_period automatic canary ramping transitions traffic per per-pin traffic allocation rules. After grace window, automatic reroute occurs using fallback_sequence unless pin is forcibly retained via customer override.

Backward compatibility: default behavior for existing pins is preserve old behavior until customer opts in. New pins default to enforce_profile_thresholds=true and a safe fallback_sequence inferred from the model catalog matchmaking service.

Data model changes (flat): add fields to Pin record: "grace_period_days", "fallback_sequence" (CSV of variant IDs), "enforce_profile_thresholds" (string "true|false"), "deprecation_notice_id".
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag gate the ledger & routing checks.
2) Internal canary: enable for internal Redwood traffic and 2 low-risk customers for 2 weeks. Monitor ledger and SLOs.
3) Beta: opt-in for selected customers (announce via CSMs).
4) Gradual enablement: rollout to 25% of pinned routes, then 50%, then 100% based on success criteria.
4b) Provide a toggle in Console per-organization to set default pin behavior.
5) After global rollout, enable automatic deprecation notices in the onboarding pipeline.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Metrics: fallback_count{pin_id,region,reason,chosen_variant}, fallback_latency_impact_ms, fallback_quality_delta_score, ledger_write_failures.
Alerts: Pager on ledger_write_failures>5m or fallback_rate_for_a_pin>10% with SLO_impact_estimate>5%.
Dashboards: per-pin timeline view, regional fallback heatmap, top-20 pins by fallback frequency, distribution of reasons (health, capacity, deprecation).
Logs: include ledger entry id in request logs for traceability.
Runbooks: incident runbook link in related_links.
Telemetry retention: 90d in Console UI; aggregated 13 months for audits.
comments: 2025-02-12 — Ava Thompson: Kickoff meeting held. Agreed on ledger append-only requirement and schema fields. Action: Ravi to prototype ledger writes.

2025-02-18 — Ravi Patel: Prototype implemented for write-ahead ledger and basic ledger viewer. Initial tests show <5ms median write latency. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/318

2025-02-25 — Mei Chen (SRE): Raised concern about metadata store write contention at 10k fallbacks/min. Decided to batch ledger writes where non-blocking; critical failbacks still synchronous. Action: implement batching and backpressure thresholds.
2025-03-01 — Priya Rao (PM): Updated acceptance criteria to require Console timeline and per-pin notifications for planned deprecations.
2025-03-03 — Ravi Patel: Integration tests added that simulate region outage and deprecation window. All tests passing in staging. Next: docs + runbook.
